transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's real nice to meet you. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Um, I guess what brings me in is... well, I had a little incident at work. It's nothing too terrible, I promise. I'm a personal care aide, and I really care about doing things right, you know? We had this staff meeting, and I guess I just got a little too worked up about safety. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room, using the chairs and waving my arms around to demonstrate. 

I was just trying to be helpful, to make sure everyone understood the protocols, right? But, um... I kind of couldn't seem to stop doing it, even when folks told me to sit down. I felt really embarrassed afterward. I know it probably sounds a bit much, but I just wanted to do a good job. Is it okay that I came in to talk about that?
Have you had a period of at least a few days when you felt unusually high, expansive, or euphoric?

Well, um... I guess you could say I have these stretches where I feel really bright, you know? Like I'm just fired up and everything is finally lining up perfectly for me to do my best work. It's a good feeling, honestly. I get a lot done! 

But, um... I suppose sometimes, if someone tries to slow me down or questions how I'm doing things when I'm in that zone... I might snap a little harder than I mean to. I don't mean to be difficult, I just get so focused on helping. I always apologize right away, though. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about.
During those times when you feel especially fired up, do you need much less sleep than usual?

Well, um... I guess I don't sleep quite as much when I'm feeling like that. But it's not like I'm tossing and turning or anything! It's actually really peaceful. 

I might only sleep, you know, maybe two or three hours. But I wake up way before dawn, and I honestly feel completely refreshed and ready to go. I'll just be up, making plans for my clients, getting things organized while the house is still dark and quiet. It feels really productive, to be honest. I didn't think there was anything wrong with getting a head start on the day, you know? Is... is that okay? Or is that something I should be worried about?
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people couldn’t?

Well, um... I mean, I don't see anything strange, nothing like that. But, um... I guess there are times... 

It's probably just my mind playing tricks on me because I care so much about my job, you know? Like, sometimes when I'm alone in the hallway at work, or even just at home by the laundry room, I'll hear someone call my name. Or I'll hear a resident calling out for help, clear as day. I'll drop whatever I'm doing and go running to check, because I want to make sure everyone is safe, right? But... then there isn't anybody there. 

It's just an overactive imagination, probably, right? From wanting to be a good aide? I hope you don't think I'm crazy or anything for saying that. It's just... hearing things like that, it's not a big deal, is it?
Do the times you hear someone calling your name or calling for help happen only when you're feeling especially energized or 'up'?

Well, um... I guess it doesn't only happen when I'm feeling all fired up. I mean, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is! But... there was a stretch, not too long ago, where I felt pretty calm. I was sleeping a normal amount, you know, maybe seven or eight hours, and I wasn't rushing around trying to get a million projects done. 

But, um... even during those few weeks, I still heard my name being called out in the empty hallways. And... I don't know if I should say this, but I still felt really sure that some of the other aides were, like, keeping notes on me or watching what I was doing. 

I know that probably sounds a little strange, right? I just wanted to be honest with you. It's okay that I still heard those things even when I wasn't feeling so energized, right? I hope that answers your question properly.
Have you ever needed to be hospitalized because of these symptoms?

Well, um... no, I've never been in a hospital for any of this. I mean, I've always managed to keep going to work and taking care of my residents. I wouldn't want to leave them short-staffed, you know? 

I guess sometimes things get a little... overwhelming, but I always try my best to handle it on my own. I wouldn't need to go to a hospital for something like this, would I? I'm doing okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by trying to push through it.

Have you ever had a period when your mood was so elevated or irritable that you got into serious trouble, like spending much more than usual, taking big risks, or behaving in a way that was clearly out of character?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I've ever gotten into serious trouble, nothing like that. I mean, I always try to be good and do my job right. But... I guess there are times, you know, stretches where I just feel... really bright? Like everything is finally lining up perfectly and I'm just so fired up to get things done. 

It's actually kind of a good feeling, wanting to be so productive, you know? But, um... I guess sometimes, if someone slows me down when I'm like that, or if they question how I'm doing things... I might snap at them. Harder than I mean to, honestly. I always feel bad about it after. It's just because I care so much about getting everything done right for the residents. 

That doesn't mean I'm a bad person, right? It's just a little stress from wanting to do a good job... I hope it's okay that I get a little irritable sometimes. That's pretty normal, isn't it?
Have you ever had a period of at least a few days when you felt unusually high or irritable and had much less need for sleep, but did not hear voices or have other unusual beliefs during that time?

Well, um... no, they kind of... they happened at the same time. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was totally out of control or anything! But, yeah, when I was in those stretches where I was all fired up, you know, sleeping just a couple of hours and coming up with all these big plans to reorganize the supply rooms... I was still hearing those calls. 

And, um... I guess during those times, I was also feeling pretty sure that my supervisor was, like, setting traps for me to catch me messing up. I didn't tell anyone about it because I didn't want to cause trouble. I just tried to work harder to prove them wrong. 

It's okay that those things were happening together, right? I mean, it's just because I was working so hard and maybe a little overtired... that makes sense, doesn't it? I hope I'm explaining it the way you need me to.
What is the longest stretch of time you’ve had when you felt unusually energized or irritable like that?

Well, um... it's kind of hard to say exactly. I don't want it to sound like it's been this huge, constant problem, because I still go to work and everything. But, I guess... those times where I'm, you know, super energized and only sleeping a tiny bit, coming up with all those big plans? They've kind of been... coming and going for a while now. 

Maybe... about 11 months? Give or take? 

It's not like I'm like that every single day for 11 months, though! It just sort of flares up and then settles down a bit. I always try to keep a lid on it so it doesn't bother anyone. That's not too terribly long, is it? I mean, a lot of people have stressful years where their energy is all over the place, right? I just hope I'm doing a good enough job managing it.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing or believing things like that even though your mood was otherwise completely normal?

Well, um... yes, I think so. I mean, I hope it's okay to admit that. There was a time, maybe for a few weeks, where things were actually pretty calm. I was sleeping better, you know, a normal amount, and I wasn't rushing around trying to fix all the supply rooms or feeling all that extra energy. My mood felt... fine. Just regular.

But, um... even during that calm stretch, I was still hearing those calls. My name, just out of nowhere. And... I still felt really sure that people at work were keeping notes on me, watching what I did. 

I didn't let it stop me from doing my job, though! I still showed up and took good care of the residents. I just kept it to myself because I didn't want anyone to think I was complaining or being difficult. That happens sometimes, right? Where you feel okay but your mind is just a little... stuck on things? I hope I'm making sense.
Has there been a stretch of at least six months when you were having these voices or suspicious beliefs, even if your mood symptoms were not strong the whole time?

Well, um... yeah, I guess so. If I really think about it... it's been going on for maybe around 9 months? 

I mean, the hearing my name and feeling like people are watching me... it's been about that long. But I really try not to let it get in the way of things! I just keep my head down and do my work. I don't want to make a big fuss about it, you know? 

Nine months probably sounds like a long time, but I've been handling it okay, haven't I? I mean, I haven't missed any shifts or anything. I just wanted to make sure I gave you the right timeline. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest or pleasure in things?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I have my down days just like anybody else, but... not for two whole weeks or anything like that. 

I really try to stay positive, you know? Even when things get a little overwhelming at work, I just keep pushing through. I wouldn't say I've ever lost interest in things or felt super depressed. I always make sure I show up for my shifts and do my best for the residents. That's the most important thing, right? I hope that's a good thing, that I haven't really felt that way. Does that sound okay to you?

Have you ever had a time when the voices or suspicious beliefs were present for at least two weeks while you were not having any mood symptoms like feeling unusually energized, irritable, or depressed?

Well, um... yeah, I think we might have just talked about that a little bit, but... yes. There was definitely a time when things were, you know, calmer. 

I wasn't having those days where I felt super energized or irritable, and like I said, I haven't really been depressed. I was actually sleeping a normal amount, which was nice, and I wasn't rushing around trying to reorganize all the supply closets or taking on extra projects. My mood was just... regular. 

But even during that time—and it lasted for a few weeks, at least—I was still hearing my name being called when no one was there. And I still felt really, really sure that my coworkers were keeping those notes on me. 

I hope it's alright that I'm repeating myself a little. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right and giving you all the details you need. Does that make sense, how I explained it?
During your most energized periods, have you ever felt so elevated or irritable that you needed to be hospitalized or were unable to keep working?

Well, um... hospitalized? No, no, I've never had to go to the hospital for it. I really try to manage things on my own, you know? 

But, um... as for working... well, they did actually put me on leave from the senior center. Just for a little bit! I think they just wanted me to take a breather, you know, because I was maybe doing a bit too much. And, well, I guess at home... my wife has had to remind me about some of the chores and my appointments. I haven't been keeping up quite as well as I usually do, but I'm really trying to get back on track with that! 

I've also sort of, um, pulled back a little from my friends at church. Just taking some quiet time, I guess. And I do worry a little bit about whether I can safely go back to my caregiving work... but I'm sure I'll be fine once I get things sorted out. 

I hope it's okay that I shared all that. I know it probably doesn't sound great that I'm on leave, but I'm really working hard to be better. Does that answer what you were asking?
Have you ever had a period of at least a week when you felt so unusually energized or irritable that you were clearly unable to function normally?

Well, um... I guess maybe? I mean, I wouldn't say I can't function normally, exactly. I try really hard to keep things going. But... there are these stretches, I guess, where I just feel so bright and fired up, you know? Like everything is finally lining up and making sense, and I have all this energy to get things done. 

It's actually a really good feeling most of the time! But... well, I suppose if someone slows me down or questions what I'm doing when I'm in that zone, I might... snap a little harder than I mean to. I don't mean to be irritable, I really don't. It's just that I feel so driven, and it can be frustrating when people don't see things the same way. 

I always apologize if I get a little sharp, though. I really try to be a nice person. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm difficult to be around. Does that sound like what you were asking about?
During your most energized periods, did you ever feel so unusually elevated or irritable that you needed to be hospitalized or were unable to keep working?

Well, um... I know we just touched on this a second ago, and I really don't want to sound like I'm repeating myself too much, but... no, no hospitalizations. I've always managed to avoid that, thank goodness. 

But, um, as for work... well, like I mentioned, they did ask me to take a little leave from the senior center. Just a temporary thing, really! I think I was just, you know, maybe a bit too enthusiastic and they thought a break would be good. And... well, at home, I guess I haven't been quite as on top of things as I'd like to be. My wife has had to gently remind me about some chores and a few appointments I missed. I'm usually much better about that, I promise. 

I've also kind of stepped back from my friends at church for a bit. Just needing some space, I suppose. And... I do have this little worry in the back of my mind about going back to caregiving, just wanting to make sure I'm completely ready and safe to do it. But I'm sure it'll all be fine! 

I hope it's okay that I'm sharing all this again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I answering your questions okay?
Have you ever had hallucinations or suspicious beliefs when you were not having any mood symptoms at all for at least two weeks?

Well, um... I guess... yes. There was a time, not too long ago, when things had really settled down. I was sleeping a lot better, getting my normal rest, and I wasn't rushing around trying to do a million projects at once. I felt pretty calm, honestly. My mood felt... normal, I suppose. 

But, um... even during that quiet time, for a few weeks, I... I still heard things. Just my name being called when no one was there. And... well, I still couldn't shake the feeling that the people at work were keeping notes on me. I know that probably sounds a bit strange, and I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything. I just couldn't help feeling like they were watching me, even when I was feeling totally fine otherwise. 

I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this. I just want to be honest so you can help me. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when your mood was so elevated or irritable that it was clearly not your usual self?

Well, um... I know we talked about this a little bit already, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but... yes, I suppose so. 

Like I was saying before, there are these stretches where I just feel so... bright and fired up, you know? Like everything is finally lining up perfectly and I have all this wonderful energy. It really is a great feeling, and I get so much done! But... um, if someone slows me down or questions what I'm doing when I'm feeling that way... I might snap a little harder than I mean to. 

I really don't mean to be irritable, I promise. It's just that I feel so driven and focused, and it can be hard when others aren't on the same page. I always feel terrible if I get a little sharp with anyone. I try so hard to be easy to get along with. Does that sound like what you were asking about? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
During those times when you felt especially energized, did you ever become so disorganized or impaired that you needed to be hospitalized?

Well, um... no, like I said before, I've never had to go to the hospital for any of this. I've always been able to stay out of the hospital, which I'm really thankful for. 

But, um... as far as being disorganized or... or impaired... well, I guess that might be part of why I'm here. I feel a little silly even talking about it, honestly, because I know I probably overdid it a bit. 

We were in this staff meeting, and... well, I just got so worked up and passionate about safety. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was moving chairs around and waving my arms to show everyone exactly how to catch someone, and... well, I guess I just couldn't seem to stop, even when folks gently asked me to sit down. I just had so much energy and I really wanted them to understand! 

I know it probably looked a little... much. I really didn't mean to cause a scene or make anyone uncomfortable. I just get so enthusiastic sometimes. I hope you don't think too badly of me for it. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you mean by disorganized?
Have you ever had any periods when the hallucinations or suspicious beliefs continued for at least two weeks while your mood was completely normal?

Oh, um... yes. I think... maybe I didn't explain it very well a few minutes ago, and I'm so sorry if I'm making you repeat the question. I hope I didn't confuse things. 

But yes, like I was trying to say earlier, there was that... that calmer stretch. It was actually a really nice time because I was finally sleeping normally, and I wasn't rushing around trying to do a dozen projects at once. My mood was completely fine. But... um, even then, for a few weeks during that quiet time, I still heard my name being called out when nobody was there. And I stayed pretty convinced that the folks at work were keeping notes on me. 

I know it sounds a bit silly, and I'm a little embarrassed to admit it again, but... yes, it did keep happening even when my mood was totally normal. Did I... did I answer that right this time? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
